topic: Customer resistance to AI in service
angle: Design CX automation around when customers actually want AI—not when finance wants deflection.
sourceTitle: Three Things to Know About Customer Resistance to AI
linkedinPost:
Most chatbot ROI dies on contact with a frustrated customer.

A recent piece from MIT Sloan Management Review synthesizes research on when customers accept AI in service. The pattern tracks what I see: people tolerate bots for low‑stakes, low‑emotion tasks but reject them when the issue feels risky, unfair, or personal.

Here’s my take from shipping AI in enterprise CX: design for choice, not captivity. Put a visible “talk to a human” path up front. Route high‑stakes intents (billing disputes, outages, cancellations) to humans by default. Use AI for triage, summaries, and after‑call work where it improves speed without blocking empathy.

Measure the right thing: “deflection with satisfaction,” not deflection alone. If your NPS/CSAT drops on deflected cases, you’re taxing the brand to save OPEX. Also track time‑to-human and containment only on eligible intents, or you’ll celebrate the wrong wins.

Practical rule: start with workflows where latency tolerance is high and stakes are low (password resets, simple order status). Earn trust there, then expand.

Where has customer resistance surprised you—either stronger or weaker than expected? #CustomerExperience #AIAdoption #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI
